I will also ensure that the test captures the output correctly and checks for the expected behavior more robustly.","tool":"run_test","args":{"source":"import pytest
from rich.console import Console


def test_soft_wrap_background_color():
    console = Console()
    
    # Capture the output of the first print with soft_wrap=True
    from io import StringIO
    import sys
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is on", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=True)
    console.print("still has background color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue().splitlines()
    assert len(printed_output) > 1
    assert printed_output[1].startswith('still has background color from previous line')
    assert '\x1b[' in printed_output[0]  # Check if background color is present in the first line
    
    # Capture the output of the second print with soft_wrap=False
    output = StringIO()
    sys.stdout = output
    console.print("soft wrap is off", style="blue on white", soft_wrap=False)
    console.print("correctly has no color from previous line")
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    
    # Check the output
    printed_output = output.getvalue().splitlines()
    assert len(printed_output) > 1
    assert printed_output[1].startswith('correctly has no color from previous line')
    assert not ('\x1b[' in printed_output[0])  # Check if no ANSI escape code is present in the second print"}}
